caption_used: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates using a logarithmic scale. Both pruning configurations maintain comparable perplexity below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%, after which values begin to diverge. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output configuration reaches approximately 15 while Per-Layer remains near 10^1. The most pronounced separation occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity climbs to roughly 50 while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than Per-Layer at this extreme.

raw_responses.Bulgarian: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a grouped bar chart comparing perplexity values for two pruning configurations—Per-Output (blue bars) and Per-Layer (orange bars)—across increasing sparsity rates from 10% to 80%. The horizontal axis, labeled "Sparsity Rate," displays the sparsity levels in 10% increments, arranged in ascending order from left to right. The vertical axis, labeled "Perplexity," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, with major gridlines at each order of magnitude and minor gridlines at intermediate points. For sparsity rates from 10% to 50%, both configurations exhibit comparable perplexity values, all below 10^1, with the bars for each rate being nearly equal in height. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output bar reaches approximately 15, while the Per-Layer bar remains near 10^1 (about 10). At 70% sparsity, the Per-Output perplexity increases to roughly 50, and the Per-Layer perplexity rises to approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations show a sharp increase, approaching 10^3, with the Per-Output bar slightly taller than the Per-Layer bar. The bars are grouped by sparsity rate, with each group containing two adjacent bars corresponding to the two configurations, and the legend in the top-left corner identifies the color coding for each configuration. No visual emphasis such as shading or outlining is applied to any specific bar.
